newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen mixed in slow trading on Tuesday due to a lack of fresh market leads as most major companies have already announced their first quarter earnings, brokers said.
"I don't see any significant corporate news as most of the major companies have announced their first quarter results," one broker said.
Brokers, however, said local players were likely to remain actively trading small-capitalised stocks on speculation.
Tourism services firm Bayu Buana and property firm Surya Semesta were among the most active on Monday and were likely to remain so on Tuesday due to speculation, brokers said.
Bayu had been active on various rumours including a possible take-over while Surya Semesta was said likely to be involved in a link-up with a foreign firm, brokers said.
Both Bayu and Surya Semesta have announced strong first quarter results.
On Monday, the Jakarta composite index fell 2.51 points to close at 692.50 points. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
Bayu fell 75 rupiah to 1,325 rupiah, with volume approaching 3.2 million shares.
Only a few blue-chips were on the active list, but their trading volumes were relatively very small due to a lack of foreign participation, brokers said.
Bank International Indonesia was unchanged at 1,925 rupiah, with only around 500,000 shares traded.
Bank BNI fell 25 rupiah to 1,575 rupiah with some 700,000 shares traded on profit-taking, brokers said.
